title: Why Retrying Fails: Context Contamination in LLM Agent Pipelines

paper.title: Why Retrying Fails: Context Contamination in LLM Agent Pipelines
paper.abstract:
Abstract When an LLM agent fails a multi-step tool-augmented task and retries, the failed
attempt typically remains in its context window—contaminating the next attempt
and elevating the per-step error rate beyond the base level. This context-contaminated restart phenomenon is widely observed in practice yet
entirely lacks formal treatment. We introduce the Context-Contaminated
Restart Model (CCRM) : a chain of T T tool-call steps, each failing with base
rate ε 0 \varepsilon_{0} ; after any failed attempt, the subsequent attempt operates in
contaminated context with elevated error rate ε 1 > ε 0 \varepsilon_{1}>\varepsilon_{0} . Under this model
we derive five main results. (R1) An exact closed-form formula for P ⁡ ( succeed in ≤ K ​ attempts ) P(\text{succeed in}\leq K\text{ attempts}) . (R2) A cascade-overhead
theorem giving the additional attempts Δ ​ K \Delta K incurred by contamination versus
the clean-restart baseline. (R3) An optimal budget-allocation theorem
identifying the pipeline depth T ∗ T^{*} that maximises success probability for a
fixed total budget B = K ​ T B=KT ; we prove the closed form T ∗ = B ⋅ log ⁡ ( 1 / ( 1 − ε 1 ) ) log ⁡ ( 1 / ( 1 − ε 0 ) ) T^{*}=\sqrt{B\cdot\frac{\log(1/(1-\varepsilon_{1}))}{\log(1/(1-\varepsilon_{0}))}} , with K ∗ = B / T ∗ K^{*}=B/T^{*} . (R4) An information-theoretic lower bound via Le Cam’s
method showing K CCRM K_{\mathrm{CCRM}} is tight up to 𝒪 ⁡ ( 1 ) \mathcal{O}(1) . (R5) A clean-restart dominance theorem quantifying the exact benefit of context-clearing
before retry. We validate CCRM on real SWE-bench Verified data: the IID model
overestimates pass@3 by 17.4 percentage points (98.6% vs. 81.2%), while CCRM
fits with error less than 0.001, implying a cascade ratio of ε 1 / ε 0 = 7.1 \varepsilon_{1}/\varepsilon_{0}=7.1 . Monte Carlo experiments confirm all theoretical predictions.

sections.heading: 1 Introduction
sections.text: Tool-augmented LLM agents execute tasks by planning and invoking external APIs, web search engines, code interpreters, and databases [ 9 , 6 , 4 , 8 ] . When such an agent fails a complex task, it typically retries—but the failure is preserved in its context window as history. Practitioners have documented the consequence: “early incorrect attempts remained in the conversation history and contaminated the final response” [ 25 ] ; agents “repeatedly referenced the same bad endpoint in future attempts because it had learned from its own mistake” [ 25 ] . Datadog’s 2026 engineering survey reports that 5% of all LLM call spans return errors [ 22 ] , yet no formal theory quantifies how retry contamination scales with task depth, error rate, or budget. Existing theoretical work on agent reliability studies single-run reliability [ 28 , 26 ] or empirical failure catalogues [ 11 ] , but does not model the cross-attempt contamination that defines real-world retry behaviour. We fill this gap.

sections.heading: Contributions.
sections.text: We introduce the Context-Contaminated Restart Model (CCRM) and prove: R1. Exact CCRM formula (Theorem 3.1 ). P ⁡ ( succeed in ≤ K ​ attempts ) = p 0 + ( 1 − p 0 ) ​ [ 1 − ( 1 − p 1 ) K − 1 ] P(\text{succeed in}\leq K\text{ attempts})=p_{0}+(1-p_{0})[1-(1-p_{1})^{K-1}] where p i = ( 1 − ε i ) T p_{i}=(1-\varepsilon_{i})^{T} , with complete Markov-chain proof. R2. Cascade overhead (Theorem 3.2 ). Closed-form Δ ​ K = K CCRM − K IID \Delta K=K_{\mathrm{CCRM}}-K_{\mathrm{IID}} ; a phase transition in ε 1 / ε 0 \varepsilon_{1}/\varepsilon_{0} makes Δ ​ K → ∞ \Delta K\to\infty . R3. Optimal pipeline depth (Theorem 4.1 ). For budget B = K ​ T B=KT , the unique maximiser of P ⁡ ( success ) P(\text{success}) is T ∗ = B ⋅ log ⁡ ( 1 / ( 1 − ε 1 ) ) log ⁡ ( 1 / ( 1 − ε 0 ) ) T^{*}=\sqrt{B\cdot\frac{\log(1/(1-\varepsilon_{1}))}{\log(1/(1-\varepsilon_{0}))}} , proved by minimising a log-convex objective. R4. Le Cam lower bound (Theorem 5.1 ). No policy can achieve P ⁡ ( success ) ≥ 1 − δ P(\text{success})\geq 1-\delta with fewer than K CCRM − 𝒪 ⁡ ( 1 ) K_{\mathrm{CCRM}}-\mathcal{O}(1) attempts, via a two-hypothesis construction. R5. Clean-restart dominance (Theorem 6.1 ). Context-clearing before retry strictly reduces required attempts; the exact improvement ratio is derived.

sections.heading: Relation to prior work.
sections.text: Tran-Truong and Le [ 28 ] fit absorbing Markov chains to single-run agent traces (within one attempt); they do not model restart contamination, provide no optimal control results, and give no information-theoretic lower bounds. Fan et al. [ 26 ] derive 𝒪 ⁡ ( T ) \mathcal{O}(\sqrt{T}) martingale bounds on single-run distortion in MCP pipelines; cross-attempt dynamics are outside their scope. Patel et al. [ 27 ] study consensus voting for reliability, not restart contamination. Table 1 summarises the differences. To our knowledge, no prior work models or analyses the cross-attempt cascade studied here. Empirically, reliability decay as a function of task depth has been documented at scale—Khanal et al. [ 23 ] show super-linear degradation across 23,392 episodes; Wang et al. [ 24 ] diagnose systematic failure modes in long-horizon agentic tasks, and budget allocation for tool-calling agents has been studied empirically [ 15 , 20 , 21 ] —all showing that naive retry strategies waste significant compute. None of these works provide a formal cascade model, closed-form success formula, or the information-theoretic lower bound of Theorem 5.1 . LLM agents benefit from data-efficient post-training [ 12 ] and reasoning-aligned preference optimisation with implicit tree search [ 16 ] ; such training reduces the base error rate ε 0 \varepsilon_{0} , and CCRM’s Theorem 4.1 shows this has superlinear benefit when the cascade ratio ε 1 / ε 0 \varepsilon_{1}/\varepsilon_{0} is large. Test-time compute allocation for multi-stage tasks [ 10 ] and web agents [ 18 ] show that adaptive budget distribution outperforms uniform allocation; Theorem 4.1 provides the theoretical optimum for the cascade-restart setting. Systematic failure diagnostics [ 17 , 11 ] confirm that retry contamination is among the most prevalent failure modes in deployed agents. sections.text: Verdent [ 14 ] : pass@1 = 0.761 =0.761 , pass@3 = 0.812 =0.812 (“three consecutive attempts on the same issue”—CCRM model). USEagent [ 19 ] : pass@1 = 0.332 =0.332 , pass@5 = 0.495 =0.495 (fresh independent retries). OpenHands : pass@1 = 0.268 =0.268 , pass@5 = 0.441 =0.441 .

sections.heading: IID baseline.
sections.text: USEagent: IID predicts 0.867 vs. actual 0.495 (gap 0.372). OpenHands: IID predicts 0.790 vs. actual 0.441 (gap 0.349). These gaps arise from correlated task difficulty —a distinct open problem.

sections.heading: Practical implications.
sections.text: (i) Measure ε 1 / ε 0 \varepsilon_{1}/\varepsilon_{0} via preliminary trials; use Remark 3 to check feasibility. (ii) Set T ∗ T^{*} from Theorem 4.1 . (iii) Clear context before retrying (Theorem 6.1 )—always beneficial. A fourth implication: reducing ε 0 \varepsilon_{0} via efficient fine-tuning [ 12 ] or search-aligned optimisation [ 16 ] has superlinear benefit when ε 1 / ε 0 \varepsilon_{1}/\varepsilon_{0} is large, because it simultaneously reduces ε 1 = r ​ ε 0 \varepsilon_{1}=r\varepsilon_{0} , shrinking K CCRM K_{\mathrm{CCRM}} doubly fast.

sections.heading: Limitations.
sections.text: (L1) Binary contamination; continuous decay is future work. (L2) Per-step independence within an attempt is a simplification. (L3) Early-exit pipelines change the budget accounting. (L4) Correlated task difficulty (Section 7.2 ) lies outside CCRM.

sections.heading: Connection to prior work.
sections.text: Tran-Truong and Le [ 28 ] fit Markov chains within a single run; CCRM is a Markov chain across runs. Combining both is an important open problem.

sections.heading: 9 Conclusion
sections.text: We introduced CCRM as the first formal framework for cross-attempt context contamination in LLM agent pipelines. Five theorems—exact formula, cascade overhead, optimal depth, Le Cam lower bound, and clean-restart dominance—provide both rigorous foundations and immediately actionable principles. Real SWE-bench data confirm that the IID assumption overestimates pass@3 by 17.4 percentage points, while CCRM fits with error < 0.001 <0.001 .

Keywords: LLM agent Tool use Context contamination Restart dynamics Optimal budget allocation Information theory 1 Introduction Tool-augmented LLM agents execute tasks by planning and invoking external APIs, web search engines, code interpreters, and databases [ 9 , 6 , 4 , 8 ] . When such an agent fails a complex task, it typically retries—but the failure is preserved in its context window as history. Practitioners have documented the consequence: “early incorrect attempts remained in the conversation history and contaminated the final response” [ 25 ] ; agents “repeatedly referenced the same bad endpoint in future attempts because it had learned from its own mistake” [ 25 ] . Datadog’s 2026 engineering survey reports that 5% of all LLM call spans return errors [ 22 ] , yet no formal theory quantifies how retry contamination scales with task depth, error rate, or budget. Existing theoretical work on agent reliability studies single-run reliability [ 28 , 26 ] or empirical failure catalogues [ 11 ] , but does not model the cross-attempt contamination that defines real-world retry behaviour. We fill this gap. Contributions. We introduce the Context-Contaminated Restart Model (CCRM) and prove: R1. Exact CCRM formula (Theorem 3.1 ). P ⁡ ( succeed in ≤ K ​ attempts ) = p 0 + ( 1 − p 0 ) ​ [ 1 − ( 1 − p 1 ) K − 1 ] P(\text{succeed in}\leq K\text{ attempts})=p_{0}+(1-p_{0})[1-(1-p_{1})^{K-1}] where p i = ( 1 − ε i ) T p_{i}=(1-\varepsilon_{i})^{T} , with complete Markov-chain proof. Optimal pipeline depth (Theorem 4.1 ). For budget B = K ​ T B=KT , the unique maximiser of P ⁡ ( success ) P(\text{success}) is T ∗ = B ⋅ log ⁡ ( 1 / ( 1 − ε 1 ) ) log ⁡ ( 1 / ( 1 − ε 0 ) ) T^{*}=\sqrt{B\cdot\frac{\log(1/(1-\varepsilon_{1}))}{\log(1/(1-\varepsilon_{0}))}} , proved by minimising a log-convex objective. R4. Le Cam lower bound (Theorem 5.1 ). No policy can achieve P ⁡ ( success ) ≥ 1 − δ P(\text{success})\geq 1-\delta with fewer than K CCRM − 𝒪 ⁡ ( 1 ) K_{\mathrm{CCRM}}-\mathcal{O}(1) attempts, via a two-hypothesis construction. R5. Clean-restart dominance (Theorem 6.1 ). Context-clearing before retry strictly reduces required attempts; the exact improvement ratio is derived. Relation to prior work. Tran-Truong and Le [ 28 ] fit absorbing Markov chains to single-run agent traces (within one attempt); they do not model restart contamination, provide no optimal control results, and give no information-theoretic lower bounds. Fan et al. [ 26 ] derive 𝒪 ⁡ ( T ) \mathcal{O}(\sqrt{T}) martingale bounds on single-run distortion in MCP pipelines; cross-attempt dynamics are outside their scope. Patel et al. [ 27 ] study consensus voting for reliability, not restart contamination. Table 1 summarises the differences. To our knowledge, no prior work models or analyses the cross-attempt cascade studied here. Empirically, reliability decay as a function of task depth has been documented at scale—Khanal et al. [ 24 ] diagnose systematic failure modes in long-horizon agentic tasks, and budget allocation for tool-calling agents has been studied empirically [ 15 , 20 , 21 ] —all showing that naive retry strategies waste significant compute. None of these works provide a formal cascade model, closed-form success formula, or the information-theoretic lower bound of Theorem 5.1 . Test-time compute allocation for multi-stage tasks [ 10 ] and web agents [ 18 ] show that adaptive budget distribution outperforms uniform allocation; Theorem 4.1 provides the theoretical optimum for the cascade-restart setting. Systematic failure diagnostics [ 17 , 11 ] confirm that retry contamination is among the most prevalent failure modes in deployed agents.
